question: How long does the postpartum period (puerperium) typically last?

options.A: Three months
options.B: Six months
options.C: Two weeks
options.D: Six weeks

explanation: The puerperium lasts for about six weeks (42 days) as the mother's body heals and returns to its normal, pre-pregnant state. You've got this!

question: What is a key nursing duty during the post-disaster recovery phase?

options.A: Monitoring for delayed health issues like infectious disease outbreaks
options.B: Stopping all documentation of past emergency responses
options.C: Discontinuing all community health education programs permanently
options.D: Closing down local clinics indefinitely

explanation: You got it! Even after the dust settles, crowded conditions and dirty water pose major risks, so nurses must stay alert for disease outbreaks.

question: Why is it important for nurses to understand food availability in the local community?

options.A: To teach patients how to manage supermarket finances
options.B: To trace nutritional deficiencies back to environmental supply issues
options.C: To calculate exact daily caloric needs for hospital patients
options.D: To inspect local restaurants for health code violations

explanation: Spotting why a community lacks food helps you connect a patient's poor health to wider supply problems outside their home. Great nursing insight!

question: Why is the dissemination step crucial in public health surveillance?

options.A: It serves as a legal punishment for hospitals that fail to report cases
options.B: It allows researchers to sell health data to private pharmaceutical companies
options.C: It ensures that useful health information reaches those who need to take action
options.D: It replaces the need for clinical diagnosis in remote rural clinics

explanation: Collecting data is useless if the findings are not shared with the people and leaders who can implement control measures. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T3#GNS313_U4_T3_h3)

question: What happens when vaccination rates drop significantly below the herd immunity threshold in a population?

options.A: The natural immunity of citizens automatically increases
options.B: Outbreaks of vaccine-preventable diseases become likely
options.C: Passive immunity replaces the need for community protection
options.D: Viruses instantly mutate into harmless strains

explanation: Falling below the threshold leaves too many susceptible hosts, allowing infectious diseases to spread easily and spark outbreaks. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T8#GNS313_U1_T8_h5)

question: What is the most common way people get poisoned right inside their own homes?

options.A: Ingestion
options.B: Injection
options.C: Inhalation
options.D: Absorption

explanation: Well done! Swallowing things—like accidental medications or household cleaners—is by far the top way poisoning happens at home.

question: Why must nurses be careful when evaluating pain in older adult patients?

options.A: Older adults do not experience acute nociceptive pain.
options.B: Older adults always report pain at a much higher intensity than young adults.
options.C: Standard rating scales cannot be understood by anyone over age sixty-five.
options.D: Pain should never be assumed to be a normal, expected part of aging.

explanation: Never brush off pain just because someone is elderly. Assuming it's 'just old age' leads to missing treatable problems!

question: Why does a person's heart beat faster when they have severe anaemia?

options.A: To warm up body tissues chilled by slow blood flow
options.B: To compensate for lower oxygen delivery by pumping blood faster
options.C: To lower high blood pressure from extra red blood cells
options.D: To help the kidneys filter out waste quickly

explanation: Think of it this way: since each drop of blood carries less oxygen, the heart has to pump much faster to make sure vital organs get what they need!

question: A patient arrives at the clinic with severe vomiting and dehydration. Why is an IV line started instead of just giving them oral rehydration drinks?

options.A: The patient's digestive tract cannot absorb any liquids safely.
options.B: Oral fluids take too long to reach the stomach lining.
options.C: IV fluids rapidly restore circulating blood volume and correct electrolytes.
options.D: Intravenous fluids taste much better than oral rehydration salts.

explanation: Great thinking! When someone is vomiting heavily, IV fluids are the quickest way to restore circulating blood volume and get their electrolytes balanced safely.

question: What is a classic ultrasound finding in someone with long-standing chronic glomerulonephritis?

options.A: Normal kidney size
options.B: Small, shrunken kidneys
options.C: A single missing kidney
options.D: Enlarged, fluid-filled cysts

explanation: Years of tissue scarring and nephron loss cause the kidneys to physically lose mass and shrink down, which doctors and sonographers easily spot on scans.

question: A nurse takes time to explain a new diabetic diet to a confused patient and their family. What role is this nurse performing?

options.A: Radiologist
options.B: Laboratory technician
options.C: Facility director
options.D: Educator

explanation: Teaching patients and families how to manage their health and care for themselves at home is a core part of our educator role. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h5)

question: Why do nurses prefer IV medications over oral tablets during severe emergencies?

options.A: It is completely painless for the patient
options.B: It delivers medication directly into the bloodstream for fast action
options.C: Oral medications are illegal in hospital emergency units
options.D: It eliminates the need for any dosage calculations

explanation: IV meds skip the digestive system completely, hitting the bloodstream instantly when every single second counts.

question: What is the main chemical powder used to make a Plaster of Paris cast?

options.A: Calcium carbonate flakes
options.B: Magnesium sulfate paste
options.C: Calcium sulfate hemihydrate
options.D: Sodium chloride crystals

explanation: Dry Plaster of Paris is made of calcium sulfate hemihydrate. When you mix it with water, it changes into a dihydrate form and hardens!

question: What is the absolute first safety step a nurse must take before asking a patient about abuse?

options.A: Have another nurse witness the conversation
options.B: Administer a full neurological examination
options.C: Ensure the alleged abuser is out of the room
options.D: Notify local law enforcement immediately

explanation: Safety first! Never ask screening questions in front of the suspected abuser, or you could put the patient in immediate physical danger.

question: What is the main job of the cerebrospinal fluid floating in the subarachnoid space?

options.A: To produce white blood cells for the nervous system
options.B: To anchor the spinal vertebrae to the spinal cord
options.C: To cushion the spinal cord against sudden physical shocks
options.D: To transmit electrical impulses directly to the muscles

explanation: Spot on! Cerebrospinal fluid acts like a built-in waterbed, protecting your delicate central nervous tissue from bumps and sudden movements.

question: What equipment do you attach directly to an oxygen source to control how fast the gas flows?

options.A: Pressure gauge
options.B: Pulse oximeter
options.C: Flow meter
options.D: Humidifier bottle

explanation: The flow meter is your best friend for control—it lets you accurately dial in the exact liters per minute prescribed for your patient.

question: What is the main problem in the body when someone has anaemia?

options.A: Increased thickness of the blood plasma
options.B: Rapid destruction of blood platelets
options.C: Too many white blood cells
options.D: Reduced oxygen-carrying capacity of the blood

explanation: You've got this! Anaemia simply means the blood doesn't have enough red blood cells or hemoglobin to carry the oxygen your body needs to function well.

question: A nurse is about to administer a high-alert medication like IV heparin. What should be done first?

options.A: Waiting until the end of the shift to document the administration
options.B: An independent double-check of the dose with another qualified nurse
options.C: Asking the patient to guess what the medication is used for
options.D: Hiding the medication package so other staff members cannot see it

explanation: High-alert drugs can easily cause severe harm if miscalculated. Always get a second nurse to independently verify the dose before giving it!

question: What is the single most important factor for emergency contraception to work successfully?

options.A: The time of day the client ate their last meal
options.B: The age and weight of the client receiving the pill
options.C: The brand name of the emergency contraceptive drug
options.D: The timing of administration after unprotected sex

explanation: Time is everything with emergency contraception! The sooner you take it after unprotected sex, the better it works. Don't leave it too late!

question: Students vomit and have stomach pain after eating snacks from an outside vendor near the gate. What should be done urgently?

options.A: Increasing the academic workload to distract students from illness
options.B: Replacing all classroom desks and chairs with new furniture
options.C: Inspecting and regulating food hygiene practices around the school
options.D: Canceling all physical education classes for the remainder of the term

explanation: Great job! Food poisoning from external sellers means health authorities need to step in and check food safety standards fast.

question: What is the final long-term outcome if chronic glomerulonephritis keeps progressing without control?

options.A: End-stage renal disease requiring dialysis or transplant
options.B: Permanent stabilization without medical treatment
options.C: Transition of the disease into chronic liver failure
options.D: Complete recovery of normal kidney structure

explanation: When nephrons are gradually destroyed over time, the kidneys eventually stop working entirely, meaning the patient will need dialysis or a kidney transplant to survive.

question: Why do emergency personnel perform debridement on a ragged, torn wound before stitching it?

options.A: It makes the skin numb to the pain of the needle
options.B: Dead tissue delays healing and easily breeds bacteria
options.C: It stops the patient from feeling nervous
options.D: It stretches the skin so fewer stitches are needed

explanation: Removing non-viable tissue leaves only healthy, bleeding tissue that can heal rapidly and resist infection. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T3#GNS311_U4_T3_h3)

question: A patient shows you a skin mole that has recently changed color and grown irregularly. What should you do first?

options.A: Refer the patient for a prompt medical evaluation and biopsy.
options.B: Advise the patient to monitor the mole at home for another year.
options.C: Apply a medicated topical steroid cream to mole.
options.D: Reassure the patient that changing moles are always benign.

explanation: Any changing mole or spot needs a professional check-up right away to rule out skin cancer. You are learning to protect your patients!

question: The Thomas-Kilmann conflict model is built on which two main personal behaviors?

options.A: Speed and accuracy
options.B: Assertiveness and cooperativeness
options.C: Empathy and detachment
options.D: Aggression and passivity

explanation: This model simply looks at two things: how much you push for your own needs versus how much you try to help the other person.

question: When should you avoid doing passive range of motion exercises on a limb?

options.A: When the client has a fresh, unhealed bone fracture
options.B: When the ward weather is unusually warm
options.C: When the client has a mild cold
options.D: When the client feels sleepy in the afternoon

explanation: Spot on! Moving a limb with a fresh fracture disrupts bone healing and causes severe pain. Always check for fractures first!

question: Which of these is an example of biochemical data collected during a nutrition check?

options.A: Presence of muscle wasting
options.B: Body Mass Index score
options.C: Serum albumin levels
options.D: Daily water intake diary

explanation: You got it! Lab tests like serum albumin give us hard biochemical facts about protein levels inside the body.

question: What is a major financial advantage of home health care over hospital admission?

options.A: It avoids expensive daily hospital room charges and facility overhead costs
options.B: It guarantees a monthly financial stipend for the patient's family
options.C: It makes all medical supplies and prescription drugs completely free
options.D: It removes the need for health insurance policies entirely

explanation: Eliminating hospital room and board fees significantly lowers the overall cost of treatment. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T11#GNS324_U1_T11_h3)

question: How does catching a larger amount (dose) of germs affect the incubation period?

options.A: It doesn't change anything at all
options.B: It stops the infection from happening
options.C: It makes the incubation period last forever
options.D: It usually makes the incubation period shorter

explanation: Starting with more germs means they don't need as much time to multiply before symptoms start showing. You get sick faster! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T84#GNS214_U1_T84_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT a safe thing to do when giving a patient nail care?

options.A: Washing the feet with warm water
options.B: Rounding down the deep corners of toenails
options.C: Filing fingernails straight across
options.D: Inspecting the skin between the toes

explanation: You're learning fast! Never round the corners of toenails too deep—it makes them grow painfully right into the skin (ingrown nails).

question: How does therapeutic gastric decompression help a patient?

options.A: It prevents vomiting and lowers aspiration risk
options.B: It permanently cures chronic gastric ulcers
options.C: It speeds up the digestion of solid foods
options.D: It stops bleeding inside the lower bowel

explanation: Removing excess fluid and air from the stomach takes pressure off the upper GI tract, stopping nausea and keeping fluid out of the lungs. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T3#GNS213_U3_T3_h1)

question: Why is careful preparation a must before transferring an unstable disaster patient to another hospital?

options.A: It allows the nurse to take a long break during transport.
options.B: It ensures the receiving hospital never has to buy medical supplies.
options.C: Moving patients without stabilization and monitoring can lead to rapid clinical deterioration.
options.D: Transfer paperwork is the only legal requirement in disaster zones.

explanation: Correct! Bumping along in a vehicle can dislodge lines or worsen shock if the patient isn't properly stabilized and monitored before the journey begins.

question: How does eating plenty of fiber help a patient managing diabetes mellitus?

options.A: By slowing down the absorption of carbohydrates in the gut
options.B: By directly acting as a substitute for pancreatic insulin
options.C: By accelerating the breakdown of simple sugars in the stomach
options.D: By entirely blocking the digestion of dietary fats

explanation: Fiber acts like a speed bump in the digestive tract, slowing down how fast sugar enters the bloodstream and preventing those sudden spikes after a meal.

question: What is the primary purpose of irrigating a fresh wound with normal saline?

options.A: To wash away bacteria and loose debris
options.B: To numb the pain temporarily
options.C: To close the skin edges tightly
options.D: To stop bleeding from large arteries

explanation: High-volume fluid irrigation physically flushes out contaminants that could otherwise cause a localized infection. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T3#GNS311_U4_T3_h3)

question: What is the very first action a nurse should take immediately after discovering a patient has fallen?

options.A: Immediately lift the patient back onto their bed
options.B: Assess the patient for injuries and vital sign stability
options.C: Complete an incident report for the hospital administration
options.D: Call the patient's family members to inform them

explanation: Checking for physical injury, pain, and stability takes precedence to prevent worsening any potential trauma before moving the patient. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T5#GNS324_U6_T5_h6)

question: Why do nurses need to know about crowd safety during mass gatherings?

options.A: Hospital administrators mandate that all nurses work at concerts and festivals.
options.B: Large crowds often produce sudden medical needs that can overwhelm local hospitals.
options.C: Crowd events are the only places nurses encounter infectious diseases.
options.D: Nurses are legally required to act as event security commanders.

explanation: When thousands of people gather, medical emergencies happen! Nurses play a key role in planning so local hospitals don't get completely overwhelmed.

question: Why do we use high flow rates when running an oxygen tent?

options.A: To create positive pressure that forces fluid out of the lungs
options.B: To dry out excess moisture accumulating on the plastic
options.C: To speed up the cooling unit's internal fan blades
options.D: To flush out exhaled carbon dioxide and maintain oxygen levels

explanation: High gas flow keeps fresh oxygen coming in while pushing out the carbon dioxide the child breathes out, keeping the air safe inside.

question: How does COVID-19 mostly spread from person to person?

options.A: By drinking contaminated municipal water supplies
options.B: Through the bite of infected mosquitoes and ticks
options.C: By consuming undercooked poultry and beef products
options.D: Through respiratory droplets from coughing and talking

explanation: You got it! Tiny droplets released into the air when people talk, cough, or sneeze are the main way the virus travels. Simple infection control basics!

question: What body position should a patient be in during a nasogastric tube insertion?

options.A: Trendelenburg position
options.B: Flat supine position
options.C: High Fowler's position
options.D: Left lateral position

explanation: Sitting upright in high Fowler's position aligns the airway and esophagus properly, making safe tube passage much easier. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T3#GNS213_U3_T3_h3)

question: Where are the receptors for water-soluble hormones located?

options.A: Inside the mitochondrial matrix
options.B: On the outer cell surface
options.C: Floating freely in blood plasma
options.D: Inside the cell nucleus

explanation: Because water-soluble hormones cannot cross the cell membrane, their receptors must be positioned on the outside surface. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T9#GNS211_U1_T9_h2)

question: What form of the malaria parasite does a mosquito first inject into a person?

options.A: Merozoites
options.B: Gametocytes
options.C: Zygotes
options.D: Sporozoites

explanation: Correct! Infected mosquitoes carry sporozoites in their salivary glands and inject them right into your skin and blood when they bite.

question: What is the main use of a fetal fibronectin test in the hospital?

options.A: To rule out delivery within the next two weeks when negative
options.B: To measure the precise level of maternal blood glucose
options.C: To confirm the exact gestational age in weeks and days
options.D: To detect active bacterial infections inside the bladder

explanation: A negative fetal fibronectin test is reassuring! It's like a reliable green light telling us delivery isn't happening in the next 14 days. Brilliant clinical knowledge!

question: What does interpersonal conflict mean?

options.A: Fighting between hospital management and unions
options.B: Arguments within a person's own thoughts
options.C: Disagreements between two or more individuals
options.D: Rivalry between two different departments

explanation: Interpersonal conflict simply means friction or clashing between separate people. Simple and clear!

question: A client using a combined oral contraceptive pill develops severe throbbing headaches and high blood pressure. What is the most appropriate nursing action?

options.A: Advise her to stop the pills immediately and refer her to a higher facility for evaluation
options.B: Switch her immediately to an implant at the same primary health post
options.C: Double her dose of oral contraceptive pills to balance her hormone levels
options.D: Reassure the client that headaches are normal and tell her to buy paracetamol

explanation: Severe migraines and high blood pressure are serious warning signs (MEC category 4) requiring prompt discontinuation and medical evaluation. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T029#GNS226_U6_T029_h4)

question: Where in the body would you look for multi-unit smooth muscle?

options.A: In the walls of the urinary bladder
options.B: In the iris of the eye controlling the pupil
options.C: In the muscular walls of the stomach
options.D: In the middle layer of the small intestine

explanation: Multi-unit muscle gives us fine, precise control—just like adjusting your camera lens or how your iris changes the pupil size in bright light!

question: Why is emotional and psychological support just as crucial as physical checks during teenage puberty?

options.A: Mental health counseling replaces the need for nutritional guidance
options.B: Rapid bodily changes often cause anxiety, confusion, and body image issues
options.C: Teenagers refuse physical examinations unless given psychological counseling
options.D: Hormonal surges permanently impair the adolescent's cognitive abilities

explanation: Exactly right! Teens go through a whirlwind of physical and emotional shifts, so offering a listening ear is a big part of good nursing care.

question: A young adult is admitted after taking too many sleeping pills on purpose. They are now fully awake and stable. What is your most important immediate nursing action?

options.A: Discharge the patient immediately with a prescription for vitamins.
options.B: Initiate strict suicide precautions and ensure constant observation.
options.C: Scold the patient regarding the dangers of taking medication.
options.D: Restrict all family members from visiting to maintain hospital quiet.

explanation: Just because they look physically stable doesn't mean the emotional crisis is over. Safety first—keep them under close watch and arrange mental health support right away.

question: You need to collect a swab from a visible ulcer on the labia minora. What is the correct way to do it?

options.A: Scrape the lesion until it bleeds profusely to get cells
options.B: Press the swab deeply into the underlying muscle tissue
options.C: Rotate the swab firmly across the base of the ulcer
options.D: Rinse the ulcer thoroughly with sterile water first

explanation: Gently rotating the swab right at the base of the sore picks up the exact fluid and cells where the trouble-making germs are hiding.

question: A pregnant patient says she wants to take a random herbal remedy she saw online for her heartburn. What is the nurse's best reply?

options.A: Advise her to check with her healthcare provider first to ensure safety
options.B: Suggest she stop eating completely until the baby is born
options.C: Encourage her to take a double dose to get fast relief
options.D: Tell her that all natural herbs are completely safe in pregnancy

explanation: Always guide patients to chat with their doctor or midwife before trying unverified remedies during pregnancy. Safety first!

question: What was a major focus of Nigeria's original 1988 National Population Policy?

options.A: Banning traditional birth attendants nationwide
options.B: Mandatory relocation of rural populations to cities
options.C: Providing free university education for all citizens
options.D: Setting a limit on the number of children per woman

explanation: Back in 1988, the policy tried to slow down rapid population growth by suggesting a specific target for how many children a woman should have. It faced a lot of cultural pushback, but that was the main strategy at the time!

question: Which type of food is best for adding bulk to stool and keeping constipation away?

options.A: Refined sugars and simple carbohydrates
options.B: High-fiber foods like vegetables and whole grains
options.C: Red meats and processed sausages
options.D: Highly processed dairy products

explanation: Fiber is a superstar! It adds bulk and softness to stool, helping things move smoothly through the bowels.

question: What is the main purpose of a commodity stock card in a family planning clinic?

options.A: To record the personal phone numbers of clients
options.B: To monitor inventory levels and prevent stockouts
options.C: To document detailed clinical side effects of pills
options.D: To evaluate the nursing staff's daily performance

explanation: Stock cards track the receipt and dispensing of contraceptive supplies to ensure the clinic never runs out unexpectedly. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T026#GNS226_U6_T026_h3)

question: Which tool is commonly used by nurses to check a patient's risk of developing pressure sores upon admission?

options.A: Apgar Score
options.B: Glasgow Coma Scale
options.C: Braden Scale
options.D: Pain Numeric Rating Scale

explanation: The Braden Scale is your go-to clinical tool! It checks things like moisture, mobility, and nutrition to give you a clear score of a patient's pressure sore risk. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h6)

question: When doing a quick ABCDE emergency check on a patient, what does the letter 'C' stand for?

options.A: Coughing
options.B: Circulation
options.C: Consciousness
options.D: Cyanosis

explanation: A is Airway, B is Breathing, and C is Circulation! You check pulses and bleeding here. Easy peasy!

question: Where does fertilization of the egg normally take place in the female reproductive tract?

options.A: The interstitial segment
options.B: The isthmus
options.C: The ampulla
options.D: The fimbriae

explanation: The ampulla is the wider middle part of the fallopian tube where the sperm and egg usually meet.

question: Why should community midwives collaborate with traditional birth attendants instead of ignoring them?

options.A: Traditional birth attendants outnumber all trained doctors in cities.
options.B: TBAs are often trusted first-line care providers in rural areas.
options.C: TBAs have advanced surgical degrees from university hospitals.
options.D: Government policy requires TBAs to manage major surgical operations.

explanation: Because many women naturally seek out TBAs first, working with them helps redirect high-risk cases to formal health facilities much faster. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T14#GNS225_U3_T14_h7)

question: At what point during your shift should you separate (segregate) hospital waste?

options.A: Right at the exact time and place you create it
options.B: After the cleaning staff pack the bins
options.C: When the waste reaches the hospital incinerator
options.D: During weekly environmental health inspections

explanation: Always sort your waste immediately as you generate it! Waiting until later leads to mistakes and accidental injuries. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T2#GNS122_U5_T2_h7)

question: Why is it important to tape or strap the catheter tubing to the patient's thigh?

options.A: It prevents pulling and friction injuries inside the fragile urethral canal
options.B: It eliminates the need for daily perineal hygiene care
options.C: It speeds up the rate of urine production from the kidneys
options.D: It prevents the drainage bag from filling up too quickly

explanation: Spot on! Securing the tube stops body movements from tugging on it, protecting delicate tissues from painful friction.

question: Which of these medications is a Direct Oral Anticoagulant (DOAC) that targets Factor Xa?

options.A: Rivaroxaban
options.B: Streptokinase
options.C: Warfarin
options.D: Unfractionated heparin

explanation: Rivaroxaban is a popular DOAC you'll see often in clinical rotation. It directly targets Factor Xa to stop clots right in their tracks.

question: In maternal health, what does 'morbidity' mean?

options.A: The death of a woman while pregnant or within forty-two days of delivery
options.B: The total number of pregnant women admitted to a tertiary hospital
options.C: Any infection contracted by a newborn baby during the first week of life
options.D: Any health condition caused or worsened by pregnancy and childbirth

explanation: Think of morbidity simply as the illnesses, injuries, or health struggles that happen because of pregnancy—distinct from maternal mortality, which means death. You've got this!

question: After finishing passive exercises for an unconscious patient, what is the final safety step you must take?

options.A: Take the patient out of bed and put them in a chair
options.B: Leave all side rails down so family can visit easily
options.C: Leave the bed high up so it is easy to clean later
options.D: Return the bed to the lowest position and raise the side rails

explanation: Safety first! Always drop the bed low and pop the side rails up to protect your patient from falls before you walk away.

question: Why is the intracardiac injection route hardly ever used in modern hospitals anymore?

options.A: Patients refusing to allow needles near their chests
options.B: New laws making emergency heart surgery illegal
options.C: The high cost of manufacturing long needles
options.D: The availability of safer and easier intraosseous and IV routes

explanation: Medical tech has advanced! Today's intraosseous drills and central lines deliver drugs super fast without putting a giant needle directly through the heart.

question: Why shouldn't nurse educators rely on just one single learning theory?

options.A: Students will complain if they only experience one teaching style
options.B: Different nursing skills and learning goals require different theoretical approaches
options.C: Accreditation bodies legally require schools to use all five theories
options.D: Only one theory has ever been scientifically proven to work

explanation: Nursing is diverse! Simple procedures need different teaching approaches than complex clinical reasoning, so mixing theories gives the best results.

question: A nursing unit spends much more money on medical supplies this month than the budget allowed. How is this situation called?

options.A: A favorable variance
options.B: An unfavorable variance
options.C: A capital surplus
options.D: A balanced revenue stream

explanation: When your expenses go higher than your budgeted plan, it's called an unfavorable variance and means you need to recheck your spending.

question: Which joint is most famously affected during a first-time gout attack?

options.A: The acromioclavicular joint of the shoulder
options.B: The proximal interphalangeal joint of the index finger
options.C: The metatarsophalangeal joint of the big toe
options.D: The temporomandibular joint of the jaw

explanation: Classic nursing knowledge! The big toe joint (known clinically as the metatarsophalangeal joint) is the absolute favorite spot for a first gout flare.

question: Right after birth, during which psychological phase does a new mother focus heavily on herself and rely on others for decisions?

options.A: Taking-in phase
options.B: Letting-go phase
options.C: Taking-hold phase
options.D: Depressive phase

explanation: Great thinking! In the 'taking-in' phase right after delivery, the mum is resting, processing her birth story, and letting nurses and family take care of her needs.

question: What is a key professional duty of every nurse when it comes to injection safety?

options.A: Hiding unsafe practices to protect the hospital's image
options.B: Refusing unsafe practices and speaking up for proper supplies
options.C: Reusing needles when the hospital budget is tight
options.D: Leaving all injections to untrained volunteers

explanation: As a nurse, your primary loyalty is to safety. You have an ethical duty to speak up against dangerous shortcuts and shortages.

question: Which type of glaucoma happens suddenly and comes with severe pain because the drainage angle is completely blocked?

options.A: Angle-closure glaucoma
options.B: Secondary pigmentary glaucoma
options.C: Open-angle glaucoma
options.D: Normal-tension glaucoma

explanation: That's right! In angle-closure glaucoma, the iris suddenly blocks the drainage path, trapping fluid and causing a painful, emergency spike in eye pressure.

question: A young woman comes to the clinic with a rigid, painful abdomen and shoulder pain after visiting an unlicensed place. What is the most likely issue?

options.A: Normal physiological postpartum recovery
options.B: Uterine perforation with peritonitis
options.C: Acute urinary tract infection
options.D: Uncomplicated incomplete abortion

explanation: A board-like, rigid tummy and shoulder pain mean internal bleeding is irritating the lining of the abdomen (peritoneum). This needs urgent surgical care!

question: What is a common result of low health literacy when it comes to family planning?

options.A: Immediate adoption of modern birth control methods
options.B: Increased funding for community health education
options.C: Spread of myths and misconceptions about contraception
options.D: Better understanding of pregnancy danger signs

explanation: When health information is scarce or hard to understand, false stories and rumors easily take over. This is why our patient education role is so vital! [learn more](GNS216_U1_T6#GNS216_U1_T6_h3)

question: What is the primary contribution of local health workers to a school health programme?

options.A: Providing clinical expertise and conducting health screenings
options.B: Drafting the national educational curriculum for science
options.C: Enforcing school discipline and attendance policies
options.D: Building new classroom blocks and administrative offices

explanation: Nurses and community health extension workers bring professional medical knowledge to evaluate student health and manage basic interventions. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T6#GNS225_U4_T6_h2)

question: Why do nurses need to assist some patients with feeding?

options.A: To ensure adequate nutrition for patients who cannot feed themselves
options.B: To completely eliminate the risk of choking during every meal
options.C: To speed up meal times in busy hospital wards
options.D: To test the patient's swallowing reflexes before discharge

explanation: You've got this! Assisted feeding is simply stepping in to help patients who aren't able to eat on their own yet, making sure they get the strength they need.

question: Why is documenting telephone orders from a physician crucial in home care?

options.A: It serves as a receipt for the pharmacy to give discounts to the client
options.B: It allows the nurse to prescribe medications independently without a doctor
options.C: It protects the nurse legally and ensures clear instructions are followed without miscommunication
options.D: It is only done to impress visiting supervisors during an audit

explanation: Documenting who gave the order, when, and the exact details prevents dangerous medication errors and provides a clear audit trail. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h6)

question: What is the main goal of a nursing assessment during the menopausal transition?

options.A: To prescribe hormone replacement therapy based on lab values
options.B: To halt the aging process and restore ovarian function
options.C: To evaluate symptom severity, overall health risks, and emotional well-being
options.D: To diagnose underlying psychiatric disorders independently

explanation: As nurses, we look at the whole picture—how symptoms affect her daily life, her health, and her feelings—to give the best support.

question: How do chronic stressors differ from acute stressors?

options.A: Chronic stressors only affect psychological well-being
options.B: Acute stressors last for months or years
options.C: Chronic stressors persist over a long period without relief
options.D: Acute stressors cause no physiological response

explanation: Think of acute stress as a sudden flash flood (short and intense), while chronic stress is like a long-term drought that wears you down over months or years.

question: What simple comfort measure can a nurse suggest for a patient dealing with dry mouth from these drugs?

options.A: Take small sips of water often or suck on sugarless sweets
options.B: Stop drinking all fluids for the rest of the day
options.C: Take your medication right before doing heavy exercise
options.D: Rinse your mouth with strong salt water every single hour

explanation: Brilliant nursing care! Frequent sips of water or sugarless candy keep those mucous membranes nice and comfortable without messing with their blood sugar.

question: What is the emergency procedure where a tiny cut is made in the neck membrane to open a blocked airway?

options.A: Removing a tracheostomy tube
options.B: Bronchoscopy
options.C: Cricothyroidotomy
options.D: Thoracentesis

explanation: A cricothyroidotomy is an emergency lifesaving move. When nothing else works and the upper airway is fully shut, healthcare providers cut through the cricothyroid membrane to create a direct path for air.

question: What happens in the body when a drug reaches 'steady-state' during regular dosing?

options.A: The drug stops working because the liver destroys all remaining molecules
options.B: The rate of drug intake equals the rate of drug elimination
options.C: The concentration in the blood continues to climb infinitely
options.D: Absorption drops to zero while excretion speeds up rapidly

explanation: Steady-state is a sweet spot! It means the amount of drug you take in matches the amount your body clears out, keeping your therapeutic blood levels nice and stable.

question: What is a crucial first step for nurses who want to provide gender-sensitive care?

options.A: Changing the legal laws of the country immediately
options.B: Ignoring all cultural traditions practiced by patients
options.C: Prescribing higher doses of medication to male patients
options.D: Reflecting on personal cultural biases and stereotypes

explanation: Exactly! Self-reflection helps us spot our own hidden biases so we can treat every patient with professional respect.

question: What is the biggest flaw in relying too strictly on the Kubler-Ross stages?

options.A: Grief is not a rigid, universal checklist
options.B: It was proven false by lab blood tests
options.C: Patients never experience anger or depression
options.D: It only works for children with cancer

explanation: Every patient handles grief differently. Treating these stages like strict rules can make us miss the person right in front of us.

question: Why must nurses change bed linens with extra care during Gallows traction?

options.A: To stop the baby from rolling onto their stomach
options.B: To keep the fracture and traction setup perfectly aligned
options.C: To keep the weights from breaking
options.D: To save money on hospital laundry

explanation: Any sudden shake can disturb the healing bone and cause great pain. Smooth, careful movements are key!

question: Why is it important for community health workers to know each other's roles clearly?

options.A: To reduce the number of home visits required each week
options.B: To prevent missed tasks and avoid doing the exact same work
options.C: To allow nurses to prescribe medications legally
options.D: To ensure doctors maintain authority over all other workers

explanation: Well done! Knowing who does what keeps care smooth and ensures no important patient need slips through the cracks.

question: When a person suddenly faces a scary or stressful situation, what is the first stage of the body's stress response called?

options.A: Alarm reaction
options.B: Exhaustion phase
options.C: Recovery period
options.D: Resistance stage

explanation: That sudden rush you feel when startled? That's the alarm reaction! It's your body's immediate fight-or-flight kick-start to help you handle sudden stress. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T15#GNS123_U3_T15_h1)

question: Why are fungal infections sometimes trickier to treat than bacterial infections?

options.A: Antifungal drugs cannot dissolve in human blood
options.B: Fungi multiply much faster than bacterial cells
options.C: Bacterial cell walls are made of strong chitin
options.D: Fungi share a close cellular structure with human cells

explanation: You got it! Because both fungi and human cells are eukaryotes, it's harder to find drugs that kill the fungus without harming our own cells.

question: A 32-year-old commercial bus driver presents with low sperm motility. Which lifestyle factor is most likely contributing to his condition?

options.A: Engaging in high-intensity cardiovascular endurance training
options.B: Prolonged daily sitting causing chronic scrotal heat elevation
options.C: Working in high-altitude environments for many hours
options.D: Consuming excessive amounts of dietary protein supplements

explanation: Professionals who sit for long hours often experience increased scrotal temperatures, which harms sperm quality. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h5)

question: Which care delivery system assigns specific tasks, like giving out meds or doing wound dressings, to different nurses?

options.A: Functional nursing
options.B: Total patient care
options.C: Case management
options.D: Primary nursing

explanation: Spot on! Functional nursing divides the workload by specific tasks across the whole ward, like a factory assembly line for care.

question: Why are local drama and folk media effective strategies in community mobilisation?

options.A: They provide a strict legal punishment for people who ignore health advice
options.B: They communicate health messages using culturally familiar and engaging entertainment
options.C: They force the government to release emergency healthcare funds instantly
options.D: They replace the need for any professional medical staff in the clinic

explanation: Drama and songs capture attention and break down complex health ideas into relatable stories. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T1#GNS124_U4_T1_h6)

question: What type of energy does an ultrasound machine use to create images inside the body?

options.A: Sound waves
options.B: Magnetic fields
options.C: Radioactive tracers
options.D: X-ray radiation

explanation: Ultrasound uses safe, high-frequency sound waves that bounce off your tissues to form a picture, meaning there's no radiation involved at all!

question: Why do different health workers come together as a team in community health?

options.A: To address complex health and social needs
options.B: To place full control of care on physicians
options.C: To reduce the number of working nurses
options.D: To lower the cost of running hospital wards

explanation: You've got this! Community health involves many overlapping social and physical issues, so different experts team up to tackle them all together.

question: What is a major social barrier that stops young people from visiting a health clinic?

options.A: Lack of electricity in the clinic waiting room
options.B: Excessive availability of free medication
options.C: Too many books in the facility library
options.D: Fear of being judged or stigmatized by healthcare workers

explanation: Nobody wants to be lectured or looked down on. When health workers show moralizing attitudes, young people stay far away from the clinic.

question: Which detail is essential to include when charting after suctioning a patient?

options.A: Color, consistency, and amount of the removed secretions
options.B: The exact brand name of the sterile gloves used
options.C: The name of the company that manufactured the suction machine
options.D: The room temperature at the moment of the procedure

explanation: Recording the characteristics of mucus gives vital clues about infection, hydration status, and overall lung health. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T12#GNS212_U2_T12_h7)

question: What is the clinical term for a fever or high body temperature?

options.A: Anoxia
options.B: Pyrexia
options.C: Hyperemia
options.D: Hypothermia

explanation: Spot on! Pyrexia is simply the medical word for a fever when your body's thermostat is temporarily turned up.

question: Why should you as a nurse encourage older patients to do tasks themselves instead of doing everything for them?

options.A: To reduce the total number of nursing staff needed on duty
options.B: To speed up the hospital discharge paperwork process
options.C: To comply with strict hospital punishment regulations
options.D: To prevent rapid physical deconditioning and loss of ability

explanation: Spot on! When older adults stop moving and doing things, their muscles weaken very fast. Encouraging self-care keeps them strong and mobile.

question: Which of these is NOT a common place to insert an arterial line?

options.A: Subclavian vein
options.B: Brachial artery
options.C: Radial artery
options.D: Femoral artery

explanation: Great eye! The subclavian vessel is a vein, while the radial, femoral, and brachial sites are all major arteries we use in clinical practice.

question: Why do patients with long-term kidney disease often suffer from severe anemia?

options.A: Damaged kidneys fail to produce enough erythropoietin
options.B: Uremic toxins coat the lungs and prevent oxygen uptake
options.C: The renal tubules destroy mature red blood cells directly
options.D: High blood pressure causes red blood cells to burst

explanation: Makes complete sense! If the kidneys are damaged, they can't make enough EPO, so the bone marrow doesn't get the signal to pump out fresh red blood cells.

question: How do the ureters move urine down from the kidneys into the bladder?

options.A: By creating high pressure using active ciliated cells
options.B: By relying solely on stretchy downward pull of gravity
options.C: By passive diffusion through tiny microscopic pores
options.D: By rhythmic muscular contractions known as peristalsis

explanation: Even if you are lying flat on your back, urine still moves to your bladder! The walls of the ureters squeeze in waves called peristalsis to push it along.

question: Which injection route is standard for administering the Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) vaccine to a newborn?

options.A: Deep intravenous bolus injection into a peripheral vein
options.B: Intramuscular injection into the thigh muscle
options.C: Intradermal injection to create a shallow skin wheal
options.D: Subcutaneous injection into the fatty arm tissue

explanation: BCG is given intradermally into the superficial layers of the skin, typically on the upper arm, producing a characteristic small raised bleb. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h6)

question: Why is it so crucial for a community nurse to track and report disease numbers quickly?

options.A: It prevents patients from visiting traditional healers
options.B: It guarantees immediate promotion within the nursing profession
options.C: It allows for early detection and rapid containment of disease outbreaks
options.D: It removes the need for community health education programs

explanation: Well done! Catching an unusual spike in illnesses early helps public health teams jump in and stop an outbreak before it goes wild.

question: What does the term 'anovulation' mean in reproductive health?

options.A: Painful menstrual cramps during a normal period
options.B: The complete absence of a uterus from birth
options.C: The failure of the ovaries to release an egg
options.D: The early cessation of all menstrual bleeding

explanation: An-ovulation simply means 'without ovulation'—the cycle happens, but the ovaries don't release an egg that month.

question: Which patient factor would usually make someone a poor candidate for deep brain stimulation surgery?

options.A: Significant cognitive impairment or dementia
options.B: Intolerable side effects from oral levodopa therapy
options.C: Severe motor fluctuations and on-off periods
options.D: Persistent resting tremor despite high medication doses

explanation: Surgery like DBS requires a clear mind to handle the device and follow-up care. If a patient already has severe memory or thinking issues (dementia), the surgery can sometimes make those worse.

question: Which human cell receptors does SARS-CoV-2 mainly latch onto?

options.A: Cholinergic receptors
options.B: Insulin receptors
options.C: ACE2 receptors
options.D: Beta-adrenergic receptors

explanation: ACE2 receptors are found in large amounts in our lung tissue, making them the main doorway for the virus to enter the body. Keep it up! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T12#GNS214_U1_T12_h2)

question: What happens to a client's bone mineral density after she stops using injectable contraceptives?

options.A: It continues to drop rapidly until old age
options.B: It turns into permanent brittle bone disease instantly
options.C: It recovers fully over time after discontinuation
options.D: It remains permanently low

explanation: Bone density might dip a bit during use due to lower estrogen, but studies show the bone mass builds right back up once injections are stopped!

question: Why must a nurse always use the exact liquid diluent provided by the manufacturer when mixing a powdered vaccine?

options.A: Using regular sterile water will cause the glass vial to shatter
options.B: Manufacturer diluents are flavored to reduce pediatric pain
options.C: Normal saline permanently stains the child's skin blue
options.D: The correct diluent ensures proper chemical balance and safety

explanation: Spot on! Mixing with the wrong fluid can ruin the vaccine or make it unsafe for the patient.

question: When considering a vaginal birth for twins, what position must the first twin be in?

options.A: Footling presentation
options.B: Breech presentation
options.C: Transverse lie
options.D: Cephalic presentation

explanation: Great job! A head-first (cephalic) position for the first baby is usually the green light doctors look for before trying a safe vaginal delivery.

question: Two days after a punch biopsy, a patient calls to say there is a firm, painful, purple lump right under their stitches. What likely happened?

options.A: Normal epithelialization
options.B: Superficial epidermal cyst
options.C: Hematoma formation
options.D: Suture hypersensitivity

explanation: When blood gets trapped and pools under the closed skin, it forms a tender, purple bump called a hematoma.

question: Giving routine childhood immunizations falls under which level of prevention?

options.A: Secondary prevention
options.B: Quaternary prevention
options.C: Tertiary prevention
options.D: Primary prevention

explanation: Primary prevention stops a disease or condition from occurring in the first place through measures like vaccination and health education. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h4)

question: What is the main focus of quantitative research?

options.A: Historical observation of ancient medical texts
options.B: Open-ended interviews about emotional trauma
options.C: Numerical measurement and statistical analysis
options.D: Detailed personal stories of patient suffering

explanation: Quantitative research is all about numbers, counting, and statistics. If you can measure it, it's quantitative!

question: Which of these is a major red flag and established risk factor for postpartum haemorrhage?

options.A: A history of previous postpartum haemorrhage
options.B: Delivery of a single low birth weight baby
options.C: Maternal age under 20 years
options.D: A very short first stage of labour

explanation: If a mother had PPH in a past delivery, she has a higher chance of experiencing it again. Always check her past obstetric history during admission!

question: What is a classic warning sign that a patient might have pulmonary tuberculosis?

options.A: Painful ulcers forming inside the oral cavity
options.B: Yellow discoloration of the sclera and skin
options.C: Sudden swelling of the lower extremities
options.D: A persistent cough lasting more than two weeks

explanation: That's right! Whenever a patient walks in with a cough that just won't quit for over two weeks, TB should immediately pop into your nursing mind.

question: What is the main risk of waiting until a six-week check-up to start birth control?

options.A: The patient may experience an unplanned pregnancy before the visit
options.B: The body will reject hormonal methods after six weeks
options.C: The patient's natural hormone levels will drop permanently
options.D: It becomes illegal to prescribe birth control then

explanation: Since ovulation can return in just two weeks, waiting six weeks leaves a huge window for another unintended pregnancy.

question: Which home modification is most helpful for preventing bathroom falls?

options.A: Placing soft throw rugs on the tile floor
options.B: Installing grab bars and non-slip mats
options.C: Using dim lighting to avoid harsh glares
options.D: Keeping the bathroom door locked at night

explanation: Wet bathroom surfaces are extremely slick, making grab bars and non-slip mats essential safety additions. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T5#GNS324_U6_T5_h3)

question: What specific cells in the human body does HIV primarily attack and destroy?

options.A: CD4+ T-lymphocytes
options.B: Neutrophils
options.C: Red blood cells
options.D: Platelets

explanation: HIV specifically targets and destroys CD4+ T-lymphocytes, which weakens the immune response over time. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T4#GNS214_U1_T4_h1)

question: What is the typical age range generally used to define adolescence?

options.A: 2 to 10 years
options.B: 18 to 25 years
options.C: 5 to 12 years
options.D: 10 to 19 years

explanation: Adolescence is widely defined by health organizations as the transitional period from childhood to adulthood occurring between ages 10 and 19. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T3#GNS312_U3_T3_h1)

question: Why do doctors often start a fast-acting anticoagulant alongside warfarin during the first few days?

options.A: Combining both drugs permanently cures chronic heart conditions
options.B: The patient's liver needs extra heparin to absorb the warfarin pills properly
options.C: Warfarin takes several days to work, so bridging prevents a dangerous gap in protection
options.D: Warfarin causes immediate thick clotting before it starts working

explanation: Warfarin takes a few days to kick in fully. Giving an injection alongside it at first acts as a bridge so the patient isn't left unprotected!

question: Why is it a good idea to soak a patient's nails in warm water before trimming them?

options.A: It softens the hard nail plate and cuticles for easier trimming
options.B: It permanently kills all bacteria hiding under the nail bed
options.C: It stops the patient from feeling any cold drafts in the room
options.D: It opens up the pores so the skin absorbs extra vitamins

explanation: Spot on! Warm water softens up the hard keratin, making clipping smooth and saving your patient from painful splits or cracks.

question: What is the primary long-term clinical use for thiazide diuretics?

options.A: Reducing intracranial pressure
options.B: Treating severe pulmonary edema
options.C: Treating chronic hypertension
options.D: Reversing acute kidney failure

explanation: Thiazides provide a steady, mild diuretic and blood vessel relaxing effect, making them standard first-line therapy for high blood pressure. [learn more](GNS223_U8_T1#GNS223_U8_T1_h4)

question: What is cervicitis?

options.A: Infection of the uterine lining
options.B: Inflammation of the cervix
options.C: Overgrowth of normal vaginal flora
options.D: Scarring of the fallopian tubes

explanation: Cervicitis refers specifically to the inflammation of the mucosal and epithelial tissues of the cervix. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T14#GNS216_U5_T14_h1)

question: How do standard antacids give quick relief from heartburn and ulcers?

options.A: Chemically neutralizing existing acid in the stomach
options.B: Creating a physical barrier over the ulcer crater
options.C: Killing the bacteria that cause stomach ulcers
options.D: Stopping parietal cells from manufacturing new acid

explanation: Antacids act like a chemical sponge, directly neutralizing the acid that is already sitting in the stomach and causing that burning feeling.

question: How does being severely underweight most often lead to fertility challenges in women?

options.A: By destroying existing ovarian follicles immediately
options.B: By halting ovulation through hypothalamic suppression
options.C: By causing physical blockage of the fallopian tubes
options.D: By thickening the cervical mucus permanently

explanation: Makes total sense, right? Extremely low body fat confuses the brain's hormone signals, which pauses the menstrual cycle and stops the release of eggs. You're doing amazing!

question: Why is a patient who just received a neuromuscular blocker at high risk for aspiration?

options.A: The drug actively causes the stomach to produce large amounts of acid
options.B: The patient's blood pressure drops so low that fluid backs up into the lungs
options.C: Patients always vomit forcefully as the paralyzing medication wears off
options.D: Complete loss of muscle tone leaves the airway and swallowing reflexes unprotected

explanation: Without working swallowing and coughing reflexes, stomach contents can easily slip into the lungs. Nursing vigilance is key here!

question: What does the intraarticular route of medication administration involve?

options.A: Delivering drugs through the skin using a patch
options.B: Swallowing pills for systemic joint relief
options.C: Administering medicine into a muscle belly
options.D: Injecting medication directly into a joint space

explanation: Intraarticular simply means putting the drug straight inside the joint cavity. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T9#GNS125_U3_T9_h1)

question: When doing a nutrition check, why does a nurse look closely at a patient's skin, hair, and nails?

options.A: To look for physical signs of vitamin and mineral deficiencies
options.B: To determine the patient's blood pressure baseline
options.C: To measure the exact percentage of body fat
options.D: To confirm the presence of contagious bacterial infections

explanation: Because parts of the body that grow fast (like hair and nails) show early warning signs when we are lacking key vitamins!

question: What is a core duty of a nurse-midwife in promoting safe motherhood?

options.A: Avoiding community engagement activities
options.B: Focusing exclusively on administrative paperwork
options.C: Providing respectful maternity care and screening during antenatal visits
options.D: Discouraging women from visiting modern hospitals

explanation: As a nurse-midwife, you are a frontline hero! You screen mums, teach them what to expect, and always treat them with love and dignity.

question: Why is accurate data management critical for preventing vaccine stockouts?

options.A: It helps health workers calculate exact needs and order correct quantities
options.B: It prevents refrigerators from losing power during storms
options.C: It stops patients from asking for unnecessary medications
options.D: It proves to international donors that nurses are working hard

explanation: Good records show how many doses are actually used, allowing clinics to order enough stock without running out or wasting supplies. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T71#GNS214_U1_T71_h8)

question: Which medical gases are usually piped right into the walls of an operating room?

options.A: Compressed steam and cooking gas
options.B: Methane, nitrogen, and propane
options.C: Carbon dioxide, helium, and hydrogen
options.D: Oxygen, nitrous oxide, and medical air

explanation: Correct! Wall pipelines supply essential life-support and anesthetic gases directly so the team always has what they need.

question: What is the final goal of the blood clotting (coagulation) cascade?

options.A: Breakdown of mature red blood cells by spleen macrophages
options.B: Conversion of soluble fibrinogen into insoluble fibrin threads
options.C: Release of erythropoietin from the renal cortex
options.D: Rapid constriction of smooth muscle in the heart ventricles

explanation: Brilliant! The whole clotting chain reaction ends by turning liquid fibrinogen into a tough, solid net of fibrin fibers that seals up the cut.

question: When it comes to formatting your paper, what golden rule connects your in-text citations and reference list?

options.A: Every in-text citation must match an entry in the reference list
options.B: Only textbooks published before the year 2000 need to be referenced
options.C: References must be completely different from the in-text citations
options.D: References should be listed in alphabetical order without citations

explanation: Good academic practice means if you cite someone in your paragraph, their full details must show up in your reference list at the end. No missing links!

question: What three factors make up 'Virchow's triad' for blood clot formation?

options.A: High blood pressure, fast heart rate, and high cholesterol
options.B: Dehydration, low protein intake, and laziness
options.C: Venous stasis, vessel injury, and blood that clots too easily
options.D: Narrowed arteries, vessel spasms, and leaky valves

explanation: Virchow's triad is a classic nursing memory tool! It covers the three things that lead to clots: blood moving too slowly (stasis), damage to the vessel lining, and a hypercoagulable state.

question: When assessing the tummy (abdomen), why must a nurse listen with a stethoscope *before* pressing or feeling around?

options.A: Hospital policy strictly requires listening before touching
options.B: Palpation can alter bowel sounds and mislead the exam
options.C: Auscultation warms up the stethoscope for the patient
options.D: Palpation causes immediate severe pain in all patients

explanation: Think of it this way: if you press on the tummy first, you wake up the intestines and change the sounds! Always listen before you touch.

question: How often should a nurse check a stable HIV patient's weight to catch any nutritional drops early?

options.A: At every clinic visit
options.B: Once every five years
options.C: Only after surgery
options.D: Only when they have a fever

explanation: You got it! Checking weight regularly helps you spot trouble before it turns into severe malnutrition or muscle wasting.

question: Why do nurses love using infrared thermometers on a busy hospital ward?

options.A: It prints out a paper record automatically
options.B: It captures temperature quickly without touching the skin
options.C: It measures core temperature directly from the heart
options.D: It never needs new batteries or calibration

explanation: You'll find these handy on the ward because they let you screen patients fast without needing physical skin contact. Great for keeping things moving!

question: Which infant condition is Bryant's traction typically used to treat?

options.A: Spina bifida complications
options.B: Severe clubfoot deformity
options.C: Fractured clavicle from birth
options.D: Congenital hip dislocation

explanation: Bryant's traction gently lifts both of a baby's legs straight up in the air to help realign a dislocated hip. Nursing pediatrics made simple!

question: Which health condition can significantly delay the normal wound healing process?

options.A: Primary hypertension
options.B: Acute tension headache
options.C: Uncontrolled diabetes
options.D: Mild seasonal allergies

explanation: High blood sugar impairs circulation and white blood cell function, which slows down tissue repair and delays safe suture removal. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h3)

question: Why is teamwork across different sectors necessary when addressing the health needs of unemployed persons?

options.A: Joblessness affects multiple aspects of life that healthcare alone cannot fix
options.B: Medical clinics have unlimited funds for business startups
options.C: Nurses are legally forbidden from talking to social workers
options.D: Government agencies prefer to work in complete isolation

explanation: Correct! Unemployment involves housing, food, and financial needs that require teamwork across different community sectors. Well done! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T18#GNS225_U5_T18_h7)

question: Which emotional reaction is very common in patients right after they acquire a physical disability?

options.A: Complete indifference and forgetfulness
options.B: Grief, shock, and depression
options.C: Aggressive pursuit of extreme sports
options.D: Immediate acceptance and joy

explanation: Losing bodily function triggers a deep grief process, much like losing a loved one. Shock and depression are very normal initial responses.

question: A patient complains of a burning, shooting pain down their leg from a pinched nerve. What kind of pain is this?

options.A: Somatic pain
options.B: Visceral pain
options.C: Neuropathic pain
options.D: Acute nociceptive pain

explanation: When the nervous system itself is damaged, it often causes burning, tingling, or shooting sensations. That's classic neuropathic pain!

question: Which of the following is a common duty for nurses in a multi-sectorial disaster team?

options.A: Negotiating international trade agreements for relief goods
options.B: Directing military troop movements in the field zone
options.C: Issuing building permits for temporary shelters
options.D: Triaging mass casualties and managing field clinics

explanation: Nurses use their clinical training to sort injured patients and run emergency treatment stations. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T7#GNS315_U5_T7_h4)

question: How do food taboos against pregnant women directly affect the unborn baby?

options.A: By contributing to low birth weight and developmental delays
options.B: By increasing the likelihood of childhood asthma allergies
options.C: By causing congenital heart defects during the first month
options.D: By accelerating the closure of the baby soft spots too early

explanation: When expecting mothers miss out on nutrients due to taboos, the growing baby misses out too, leading to poor birth outcomes.

question: How is the autonomic nervous system different from the somatic nervous system?

options.A: The autonomic system is completely independent and never interacts with the brain.
options.B: The autonomic system controls involuntary organs while the somatic controls voluntary muscles.
options.C: The autonomic system only uses sensory neurons while the somatic uses motor neurons.
options.D: The autonomic system is located in the brain while the somatic is in the spinal cord.

explanation: Spot on! Somatic nerves let you move your arms and legs on purpose, while autonomic pathways handle the behind-the-scenes organs that work without your direct control.

question: What mindset must a nurse keep to successfully teach family life education to diverse groups?

options.A: Immediate judgment of non-traditional family structures
options.B: Cultural humility and freedom from personal bias
options.C: Total avoidance of sensitive reproductive topics
options.D: Strict adherence to traditional cultural practices only

explanation: Wonderful! Approaching patients with an open mind and checking our own biases lets us give respectful, non-judgmental care to everyone.

question: What two signs tell us a mother is truly in preterm labour?

options.A: Regular contractions and progressive cervical change
options.B: Complete rupture of membranes and heavy bleeding
options.C: Severe headache and blurred vision in the third trimester
options.D: High blood pressure and sudden swelling of the feet

explanation: Spotting true labour means looking for both regular tummy tightening (contractions) and signs that the cervix is actually opening up. Great job learning the clinical markers!

question: Which nitrogenous base always pairs with Adenine in a DNA molecule?

options.A: Uracil
options.B: Thymine
options.C: Guanine
options.D: Cytosine

explanation: Adenine always bonds specifically with thymine to form the rungs of the DNA ladder. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T7#GNS111_U1_T7_h1)

question: Where should the patient stand on the platform during a weight measurement?

options.A: Leaning against the wall for proper balance
options.B: As far forward as possible to see the numbers
options.C: In the exact center with weight distributed evenly
options.D: With one foot on the floor for stability

explanation: Standing centrally with balanced footing ensures the entire body mass rests squarely on the weighing mechanism. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T8#GNS225_U2_T8_h5)

question: What primary body system does an intravenous pyelogram examine?

options.A: The central nervous system
options.B: The urinary system
options.C: The respiratory system
options.D: The digestive tract

explanation: An IVP specifically targets the kidneys, ureters, and bladder to evaluate how well urine flows through the urinary tract. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T3#GNS213_U4_T3_h1)

question: Why must a community nurse look at social factors like poverty alongside clinical symptoms?

options.A: Clinical vital signs are completely useless without a university degree
options.B: Hospital management requires a list of every patient's religious beliefs
options.C: Social issues like poverty and poor housing often drive poor health outcomes
options.D: Social assessments replace the need to check blood pressure and pulse

explanation: A patient's living conditions tell half the story. If someone goes home to dirty water and no food, treating their illness at the clinic is only a temporary fix.

question: Which sign is a major red flag for pneumonia or a serious chest infection in an infant?

options.A: Swollen joints and painful movement
options.B: Yellow discoloration of the skin
options.C: Inability to close the eyelids fully
options.D: Fast breathing or chest indrawing

explanation: Well done! Breathing very fast or having the skin suck in around the ribs are classic warning signs that a baby is struggling to breathe.

question: A patient taking a strong central nervous system depressant is most at risk for which major complication?

options.A: Dangerous slowing of breathing and respiratory rate
options.B: Sudden uncontrollable muscle spasms in the legs
options.C: Extreme physical agitation and sleeplessness
options.D: Permanent elevation of body temperature

explanation: Because these drugs quiet the brain, they can suppress the brain's breathing control center. Always watch your patient's respiratory rate closely!

question: A patient with pneumonia says their chest hurts sharply every time they take a deep breath. What's the most likely reason?

options.A: Sudden spasms of the chest muscles
options.B: Extra pressure inside the right side of the heart
options.C: Inflamed lung linings rubbing against the chest wall
options.D: Irritation of the main breathing tubes in the throat

explanation: That sharp pain is called pleuritic chest pain. It happens when the inflamed outer lining of the lungs (pleura) rubs against the chest wall with every breath.

question: Why is suction applied intermittently rather than continuously during airway clearance?

options.A: To allow the suction machine time to build up mechanical pressure
options.B: To make sure the sterile catheter stays clean on the inside
options.C: To prevent severe damage to the airway lining and low oxygen levels
options.D: To give the nurse enough time to measure the suction gauge

explanation: Continuous suctioning pulls too much air out of the lungs and aggressively grips the delicate tissue inside the airway. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T12#GNS212_U2_T12_h1)

question: What are the three core principles of radiation safety?

options.A: Time, distance, and shielding
options.B: Light, sound, and pressure
options.C: Color, weight, and volume
options.D: Speed, heat, and moisture

explanation: Limiting exposure time, increasing distance from the source, and using physical shielding protect workers from harmful radiation. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T7#GNS112_U4_T7_h6)

question: What is a common misconception about the health status of adolescents?

options.A: They are naturally healthy and rarely need medical attention
options.B: They have complete immunity against sexually transmitted infections
options.C: They never experience emotional or mental health challenges
options.D: They suffer from chronic heart conditions more than older adults

explanation: Many people mistakenly assume teenagers do not need healthcare because they look strong, ignoring important preventive and mental health needs. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T16#GNS312_U3_T16_h3)

question: Which everyday Nigerian kitchen item is a powerhouse source of Vitamin A?

options.A: Polished white rice
options.B: Red palm oil
options.C: Processed wheat flour
options.D: Refined white sugar

explanation: Well done! Unrefined red palm oil is loaded with beta-carotene, which our bodies turn straight into healthy Vitamin A.

question: During which of the following periods can mother-to-child transmission of HIV NOT occur?

options.A: Postnatally while the infant is breastfeeding
options.B: Pre-conception before fertilization takes place
options.C: Intrapartum during the actual labor and delivery
options.D: In utero during the course of the pregnancy

explanation: Transmission requires active exposure during pregnancy, delivery, or through breast milk; it does not happen before conception occurs. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T11#GNS216_U6_T11_h2)

question: A patient keeps visiting the clinic with headaches and stomach upset, but all lab tests come out normal. What should you suspect?

options.A: Unresolved psychological stress manifesting as physical symptoms
options.B: A severe vitamin deficiency requiring immediate surgery
options.C: An accidental poisoning caused by community water supply
options.D: A rare tropical infection that laboratory tests cannot detect

explanation: When the lab results are completely clear but the pain is real, the body is often speaking the language of unexpressed stress (somatization).

question: Why is it so important to accurately chart the exact time and volume of a blood transfusion?

options.A: It provides a legal record of care and helps track fluid balance
options.B: It prevents the patient from receiving another transfusion ever again
options.C: It is only required for hospital billing and insurance purposes
options.D: It allows the nurse to claim overtime payment for the procedure

explanation: Good charting keeps your patient safe and protects your license! It gives a clear picture of their fluid status and serves as a legal record that you delivered safe, quality care.

question: How does cigarette smoking negatively affect the musculoskeletal system?

options.A: It makes the bones grow abnormally long and thin
options.B: It completely destroys all cartilage overnight
options.C: It causes immediate swelling in all major joints
options.D: It reduces blood supply to bones and slows healing

explanation: Smoking constricts blood vessels, which deprives bone tissue of needed oxygen and nutrients. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T25#GNS222_U1_T25_h5)

question: A patient with a leg cast complains of a sharp, burning pain in one spot underneath. What stockinette issue could be causing this?

options.A: The stockinette is too long at the top of the knee
options.B: The cotton material is absorbing too much fresh air
options.C: A wrinkle or fold in the stockinette causing pressure
options.D: The stockinette color is clashing with the plaster

explanation: Sharp, localized burning pain under a cast is a classic sign that a wrinkle or bunch in the stockinette is pressing hard into the skin. Smooth it out early!

question: What type of grief do family members often feel while watching a loved one slowly decline from a terminal illness?

options.A: Unresolved grief
options.B: Transient grief
options.C: Pathological grief
options.D: Anticipatory grief

explanation: Brilliant! Families often start mourning the loss long before it actually happens while watching a loved one fade over time. That's called anticipatory grief.

question: What should a nurse typically do after a patient gets a positive result on a screening RDT?

options.A: Start major surgery immediately
options.B: Throw away all the remaining test kits
options.C: Ignore the result and send the patient home
options.D: Perform a confirmatory test if required by guidelines

explanation: Screening tests can sometimes give false positives, so important diagnoses often require a second confirmatory test. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T4#GNS124_U6_T4_h4)

question: You want to interview patients tomorrow for a project but haven't gotten IRB ethics approval yet. What should you do?

options.A: Ask the head nurse to bypass the ethics committee
options.B: Collect data fast before anyone notices
options.C: Stop and wait until official ethical clearance is granted
options.D: Go ahead with interviews if patients give verbal consent

explanation: Exactly right! Patient safety comes first—never start human research without proper ethical clearance.

question: What do we call a public health system where workers actively visit clinics and review records to hunt down hidden cases?

options.A: Passive surveillance
options.B: Active surveillance
options.C: Tertiary surveillance
options.D: Sentinel surveillance

explanation: You've got this! Active surveillance means health workers take the initiative to go out and look for cases instead of just waiting for reports to land on their desks.

question: Why are deep yellow and orange vegetables so good for your health?

options.A: It speeds up the absorption of glucose in the gut
options.B: It binds directly to cholesterol in the stomach
options.C: It acts as a precursor to vitamin A in the body
options.D: It serves as the main structural protein for cell walls

explanation: Great job! Beta-carotene is simply a plant pigment that your body turns into vitamin A, which keeps your eyes and immune system strong.

question: Which of these is a classic sign of an acute hemolytic transfusion reaction?

options.A: Lower back pain and dark urine
options.B: Dry cough and sudden hair loss
options.C: Gradual joint stiffness and swelling
options.D: Severe itching and localized rash

explanation: When red blood cells break down rapidly inside the body, the released hemoglobin travels to the kidneys and bloodstream, leading to classic flank/lower back pain and dark, tea-colored urine.

question: How should a nurse pull the ear pinna when giving ear drops to an adult patient?

options.A: Downward and forward
options.B: Downward and backward
options.C: Upward and backward
options.D: Straight outward by the lobe

explanation: Pulling the adult ear pinna up and back straightens the curved ear canal so the drops can reach the eardrum area. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T10#GNS122_U1_T10_h2)

question: Which bar chart style places sub-category bars directly on top of each other to show a total?

options.A: Grouped bar chart
options.B: Stacked bar chart
options.C: Simple bar chart
options.D: Scatter plot chart

explanation: A stacked bar chart segments a single bar to show both individual parts and the combined total. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T7#GNS217_U4_T7_h3)

question: Which medical condition is closely linked to blood vessel smooth muscle staying too constricted over time?

options.A: Osteoporosis
