options.B: Anemia
options.C: Hypertension
options.D: Hypoglycemia

explanation: When the smooth muscle in blood vessel walls stays chronically tight, the vessels narrow and resistance climbs, which we know as high blood pressure (hypertension). Great job working through this set!

question: Which medication is most commonly used as a local anesthetic for closing minor wounds?

options.A: Lignocaine
options.B: Paracetamol
options.C: Morphine
options.D: Diazepam

explanation: Lignocaine numbs the local area quickly and safely when administered correctly before suturing. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T3#GNS311_U4_T3_h2)

question: Which part of the stethoscope is best suited for hearing low-pitched murmurs like S3 or S4?

options.A: The bell
options.B: The tubing
options.C: The ear pieces
options.D: The diaphragm

explanation: The bell of the stethoscope transmits low-frequency sounds better when held lightly against the patient's skin. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T2#GNS213_U1_T2_h3)

question: How is rheumatoid arthritis different from osteoarthritis?

options.A: Rheumatoid arthritis is an autoimmune and systemic inflammatory condition
options.B: Rheumatoid arthritis only affects a single weight-bearing joint at a time
options.C: Rheumatoid arthritis is strictly caused by heavy physical labor and aging
options.D: Rheumatoid arthritis involves no inflammation of the synovial membranes

explanation: While osteoarthritis is mostly wear-and-tear on a specific joint over time, rheumatoid arthritis happens when the immune system mistakenly attacks the joints all over the body.

question: Oops! During insertion, your catheter accidentally slips into the female vagina. What should you do next?

options.A: Wash the same catheter with antiseptic soap and try again
options.B: Leave it temporarily as a landmark and insert a new sterile catheter
options.C: Push it deeper into the vagina to find the correct opening
options.D: Remove it and immediately push that same tube into the urethral meatus

explanation: Smart nursing move! Leaving that stray tube in the vagina stops you from accidentally making the same mistake twice on your next try.

question: What happens when different tiers of government fail to coordinate their healthcare efforts?

options.A: Health interventions become scattered and ineffective at the grassroots
options.B: Private hospitals take over all immunizations
options.C: Local communities get amazing foreign medical aid automatically
options.D: Funding for special populations shoots up everywhere

explanation: Exactly! When federal, state, and local governments don't communicate well, gaps open up, and vulnerable people end up missing the care they deserve.

question: What is the key difference between active and passive infection surveillance?

options.A: Active surveillance only occurs at night, while passive surveillance happens during morning shifts
options.B: Active surveillance involves staff proactively hunting for data, while passive relies on voluntary reporting
options.C: Passive surveillance tracks viral illnesses, while active surveillance focuses only on bacterial issues
options.D: Passive surveillance uses computer software, while active surveillance is done entirely on paper

explanation: Spot on! Active means staff actively go looking for cases, while passive means waiting for someone to report them.

question: Which of these is a classic example of environmental asphyxia?

options.A: Severe diabetic ketoacidosis
options.B: An acute myocardial infarction
options.C: Drowning in a swimming pool
options.D: A sudden allergic asthma attack

explanation: Environmental asphyxia happens when outside factors—like water, smoke, or a tight space—keep a person from reaching clean air. Water in a pool is a clear external block!

question: What is the main difference between macronutrients and micronutrients?

options.A: If they come from plants or animals
options.B: The relative quantity the body needs
options.C: Whether they provide any energy at all
options.D: How fast the stomach digests them

explanation: It's all about amount! Macronutrients are needed in large amounts, while micronutrients (like vitamins and minerals) are needed in tiny amounts—though both are equally important for health.

question: Which type of small intestinal disorder involves long-term, deep inflammation of the bowel wall that can form strictures and fistulae?

options.A: Inflammatory and autoimmune disorders
options.B: Benign mucosal hyperlasias
options.C: Simple infectious enteritis
options.D: Mechanical and functional obstructions

explanation: You've got this! Crohn's disease is a great example here—it causes deep, full-thickness inflammation right through the intestinal wall layers.

question: How many escape routes should a good fire safety plan provide for each room?

options.A: As many as there are windows
options.B: Only one main front door
options.C: At least two ways out
options.D: One exit per floor level

explanation: Always plan for two ways out! If fire or thick smoke blocks the main doorway, you need a backup route like a window.

question: A patient asks why local whole grains and tubers are better than refined sugar. What is your best response?

options.A: They contain zero calories unlike refined sugar
options.B: They are imported from overseas and have cleaner nutrients
options.C: They digest instantly to give quick energy without insulin
options.D: They contain fiber that slows digestion and prevents sudden blood sugar spikes

explanation: Complex carbs and whole tubers come packed with natural fiber. This slows down glucose absorption, keeping blood sugar nice and stable.

question: A nurse wants to teach a rural community how to prevent cholera. What is the best way to communicate?

options.A: Distribute dense medical textbooks written in advanced technical English.
options.B: Post warning notices exclusively on international websites.
options.C: Use local languages and collaborate with respected community leaders.
options.D: Rely entirely on unspoken signs posted without any translation.

explanation: People listen best to trusted community voices speaking in their own language. Communication is key in public health!

question: What effect do inflammatory cytokines have on blood sugar levels during severe illness?

options.A: They cause stress hyperglycemia even without a diabetes history.
options.B: They drop blood sugar to dangerously low levels immediately.
options.C: They cause the pancreas to stop producing insulin forever.
options.D: They have no effect on how the body handles glucose.

explanation: Stress hormones and cytokines released during trauma drive up blood glucose, often requiring careful monitoring and management. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T023#GNS227_U2_T023_h3)

question: What is the golden rule for feeding an infant during their first six months of life?

options.A: Exclusive breastfeeding with no other foods or liquids
options.B: Cow milk combined with fresh fruit juices
options.C: Formula milk mixed with clean local spring water
options.D: Breastmilk supplemented with thin cereal porridges

explanation: You got it! Breastmilk alone for the first six months provides all the nutrients and infection-fighting protection a baby needs.

question: What type of liability do nurse managers usually face if they do a poor job with staffing or hiring?

options.A: Strict criminal liability for patient readmissions
options.B: Direct liability for administrative negligence
options.C: Absolute immunity from all civil court proceedings
options.D: Vicarious liability for every bedside drug error

explanation: Managers have specific administrative duties like vetting staff properly. If they fail here, they face direct liability for their own poor management.

question: What is the biggest danger when someone has a severe case of watery diarrhoea?

options.A: Sudden increase in white blood cell count
options.B: Permanent damage to the stomach lining
options.C: Complete blockage of the large intestine
options.D: Rapid loss of water and electrolytes

explanation: Frequent watery stools quickly drain the body of vital fluids and salts, which can lead to dangerous dehydration before you know it. Great job keeping watch for this!

question: What is a major practical challenge to good clinical supervision in busy Nigerian hospitals?

options.A: An excess of well-trained administrative supervisors
options.B: Complete absence of any clinical policies or guidelines
options.C: Heavy staff workloads and severe staff shortages
options.D: Too much free time available during morning shifts

explanation: We all know how packed the wards can get! High patient numbers and few staff members make it tough to find time for mentoring.

question: What is the primary tool midwives use to track the progress of labour on a chart?

options.A: Partograph
options.B: Growth curve
options.C: Bishoff scale
options.D: Apgar chart

explanation: The partograph gives us a neat visual story of how labour is going. It's our best friend for spotting slow progress or fetal distress early!

question: Which health problem is a woman more likely to face later in life if she had preeclampsia during pregnancy?

options.A: Higher lifetime risk of heart disease
options.B: Chronic chest allergies
options.C: Permanent blindness in both eyes
options.D: Getting chronic kidney stones

explanation: Having preeclampsia is like a stress test for the body's blood vessels, meaning these women have a higher chance of heart and blood pressure issues later in life.

question: How does breastfeeding help a mother's body immediately after delivery?

options.A: It prevents all future menstrual cycles permanently
options.B: It increases total red blood cell volume rapidly
options.C: It repairs perineal tears without surgical intervention
options.D: It stimulates uterine contractions to reduce postpartum bleeding

explanation: Oxytocin released during feeding makes the uterus contract, which helps close blood vessels and lowers the risk of heavy bleeding. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T015#GNS226_U3_T015_h4)

question: What type of cells normally cover the outer part (ectocervix) of a healthy cervix?

options.A: Stratified squamous epithelium
options.B: Transitional epithelium
options.C: Simple columnar epithelium
options.D: Pseudostratified ciliated epithelium

explanation: The outer cervix is covered by tough stratified squamous cells. They act like a strong shield against friction and the natural acidity of the vagina.

question: Sickle cell disease is most commonly found in people of which ancestral background?

options.A: African, Mediterranean, or Middle Eastern descent
options.B: Northern European and Scandinavian descent
options.C: East Asian and Pacific Islander descent
options.D: Indigenous Australian and New Zealand descent

explanation: Inherited conditions like sickle cell anaemia are much more common in specific ancestral groups from regions like Africa, the Mediterranean, and the Middle East.

question: What anatomical feature of the skin creates your unique fingerprints?

options.A: Dermal papillae interlocking beneath the surface
options.B: Friction of the outer skin rubbing against clothes
options.C: Sweat gland tubes branching out
options.D: Adipose tissue buildup in the lower layer

explanation: You got it! Tiny wave-like bumps called dermal papillae push up from the dermis, creating the unique patterns we know as fingerprints. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T1#GNS211_U2_T1_h3)

question: What do we call the outward, social way a person shows their grief?

options.A: Depression
options.B: Denial
options.C: Mourning
options.D: Suffering

explanation: Mourning is simply the visible, cultural, and social actions people take to express their grief after a loss.

question: What does intersectoral collaboration mean in the context of safe motherhood?

options.A: Leaving health matters exclusively to medical doctors
options.B: Closing down primary health centers to build markets
options.C: Working together with different sectors like transport, education, and health
options.D: Transferring all pregnant women to foreign countries for treatment

explanation: Maternal health is influenced by many factors outside the clinic, requiring cooperation across multiple government and community sectors. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T44#GNS214_U1_T44_h7)

question: Which group of people benefits the most from herd immunity against respiratory infections?

options.A: Young adults working in busy office buildings
options.B: Older adults who get their flu shots on time
options.C: People who are too young or have weak immune systems to get vaccines
options.D: Healthy athletes training outdoors

explanation: Herd immunity acts like a protective shield. When most of the community is vaccinated, it stops the germ from spreading to vulnerable people who cannot take vaccines themselves.

question: A patient living in a rural home with poor kitchen ventilation uses wood for daily cooking and now has a lasting cough. What is the best primary prevention advice?

options.A: Give them a course of strong oral antibiotics right away
options.B: Recommend using a quick-relief rescue inhaler every day
options.C: Order a chest X-ray to check for tuberculosis
options.D: Advise the family to switch to cleaner cooking fuel and improve kitchen airflow

explanation: Primary prevention stops the problem before it starts or worsens. Fixing indoor smoke exposure removes the root environmental trigger keeping that cough going!

question: Why is it important for nurses to know if a cancer treatment is meant to cure the disease or provide comfort (palliative)?

options.A: It dictates whether the patient is allowed to receive any form of nutrition by mouth
options.B: Palliative regimens mean the patient no longer requires physical assessments or lab work
options.C: Curative regimens require nurses to administer medications without checking vital signs
options.D: It helps guide realistic patient expectations, monitoring priorities, and supportive care planning

explanation: Great nursing insight! Knowing the main goal of treatment helps you plan the best supportive care and keep patient expectations clear and hopeful.

question: What does the integrase enzyme do in the HIV life cycle?

options.A: It destroys circulating antibodies produced by B cells.
options.B: It manufactures new outer coats for budding virus particles.
options.C: It breaks down the outer cell wall of the host lymphocyte.
options.D: It inserts viral DNA into the host cell's genetic material.

explanation: Integrase acts like molecular glue, pasting the copied viral DNA right into the human host cell's DNA.

question: As the name suggests, what does a 'mixed methods' research design mix together?

options.A: Experimental and historical approaches
options.B: Inpatient and outpatient clinical data
options.C: Quantitative and qualitative approaches
options.D: Animal studies and laboratory testing

explanation: Easy peasy! It mixes numbers (quantitative) with words and stories (qualitative) to get the best of both worlds.

question: What happens in the nervous system when an opioid binds to its receptor?

options.A: It forces the body to release high amounts of natural prostaglandins
options.B: It stimulates rapid electrical firing along nerve endings
options.C: It inhibits the transmission of pain signals to the brain
options.D: It speeds up the heart rate to increase oxygen delivery

explanation: Think of opioids as a roadblock: they stop pain messages from traveling up the nerves so your brain doesn't feel them as intensely.

question: Why are fresh flowers and live plants banned from the room of an immunocompromised patient?

options.A: They attract stinging insects into the hospital room
options.B: Their soil and standing water harbor dangerous fungi
options.C: Their strong scent can trigger severe allergic asthma
options.D: They consume too much oxygen in a closed space

explanation: Soil and stagnant water are breeding grounds for fungi and bacteria that can easily cause severe infections in patients with low white blood cells. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T15#GNS311_U2_T15_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of using screening tools like the Internet Addiction Test in nursing?

options.A: To diagnose underlying viral infections transmitted through the internet
options.B: To gather objective data on problematic technology use and its impact
options.C: To measure the exact electrical current flowing through the device battery
options.D: To permanently block harmful websites on the patient's mobile phone

explanation: Just like checking vital signs, screening tools help nurses measure how deeply technology is affecting a patient's life so we can offer the right help.

question: How should you handle your personal moral beliefs when caring for a post-abortion client?

options.A: Refuse to provide any medication or comfort
options.B: Put personal views aside to deliver respectful care
options.C: Report the client to religious leaders
options.D: Argue with the client about their life choices

explanation: Professional nursing ethics mean we always put our patient's health and dignity first, delivering unbiased, compassionate care no matter our personal background. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T007#GNS226_U5_T007_h2)

question: A new nurse is sorting waste on a busy ward. Which action shows they are following safety rules correctly?

options.A: Dropping a used syringe directly into a puncture-resistant box without recapping
options.B: Tossing blood-stained gauze into the ordinary office waste bin
options.C: Recapping a needle carefully using both hands before disposal
options.D: Storing expired medications in the ward refrigerator next to patient snacks

explanation: Brilliant! Dropping the used syringe straight into the safety box without trying to recap it is the golden rule for preventing needle-stick injuries.

question: Why must vaccine and medication storage refrigerators have their temperatures checked and recorded regularly?

options.A: To ensure the refrigerator door is locked at all times
options.B: To check if the electricity bill is too high for the ward
options.C: To make sure improper heat does not ruin drug potency
options.D: To calculate how many patients received injections that day

explanation: Many pharmaceutical products degrade quickly if temperatures fluctuate outside the safe cold chain range. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T19#GNS122_U3_T19_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common post-testicular cause of male factor infertility?

options.A: Congenital absence of the vas deferens
options.B: Pituitary tumor suppressing hormone release
options.C: Blockage of the vas deferens from previous surgery
options.D: Scarring of the epididymis from a chronic infection

explanation: A pituitary tumor is a pre-testicular hormonal issue, whereas post-testicular causes involve blockages or transport problems after sperm is made. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h4)

question: What does antimicrobial resistance actually mean?

options.A: Immune systems destroying white blood cells
options.B: The human body rejecting prescribed vitamins
options.C: Microorganisms evolving to survive standard medications
options.D: Bacteria growing faster in cold temperatures

explanation: You've got this! Resistance simply means germs change and adapt so that drugs like antibiotics can no longer destroy them.

question: What do we mean by an 'acute abdomen' in clinical practice?

options.A: Chronic indigestion caused by spicy food
options.B: Sudden, severe abdominal pain that often requires urgent surgery
options.C: A normal feeling of fullness after a large meal
options.D: A mild muscle cramp after heavy exercise

explanation: Spot on! An 'acute abdomen' is a red flag for sudden, severe belly pain that usually means trouble inside, like appendicitis or a perforation, needing quick surgical eyes.

question: Why are interdisciplinary rounds (where different health workers meet together) so helpful?

options.A: They ensure that doctors make all decisions without input from nurses
options.B: They allow multiple departments to discuss care plans together in real time
options.C: They remove the need for any documentation in the patient chart
options.D: They replace the nursing management team with administrative staff

explanation: Brilliant! Bringing everyone together at once clears up confusion instantly so the whole healthcare team is on the exact same page for the patient.

question: Which finding in an infant always requires a prompt medical checkup?

options.A: Sneezing once or twice after exposure to morning sunlight
options.B: Spitting up a small amount of milk after a burping session
options.C: A rectal temperature of 38.0°C or higher in a two-month-old
options.D: Having yellow, soft, seedy stools when being breastfed

explanation: Spot on! Any fever in a baby under three months old is an emergency. Always have it checked right away to rule out serious infections.

question: How does your blood protect your body against germs and infections?

options.A: By increasing the total volume of red blood cells
options.B: By filtering toxins directly through the skin
options.C: By lowering blood pressure during an illness
options.D: By circulating white blood cells and antibodies

explanation: Exactly! Your bloodstream acts like a highway, rushing white blood cells and antibodies straight to wherever germs are trying to attack.

question: Why do nurses and doctors pay very close attention when a lab report mentions dysplasia?

options.A: It guarantees that the tissue has already formed a malignant tumor
options.B: It causes immediate and total loss of function in the affected organ
options.C: It means the cells have permanently shrunk due to prolonged starvation
options.D: It represents disordered cellular growth that can progress to cancer

explanation: Dysplasia means the cells are looking disorganized and weird. Catching this early is key because it can sometimes turn into cancer if the stress doesn't stop.

question: What is the normal pH range for human blood?
explanation: Spot on! Blood pH is tightly kept between 7.35 and 7.45 so that enzymes and vital body processes can run smoothly.

question: When caring for a patient with a cast, why should a nurse assess the whole patient and not just stare at the injury?

options.A: To ensure the plaster cast does not get dirty or wet
options.B: To monitor for dangerous systemic changes affecting the whole body
options.C: To measure the exact length of the bone healing underneath
options.D: To check if the patient is taking their pain medication on time

explanation: A bone injury doesn't happen in isolation! It can trigger widespread reactions throughout the body, so looking at the big picture helps you catch complications early.

question: Why does kidney compensation take longer than lung compensation during an acid-base imbalance?

options.A: Kidneys must slowly adjust tubular secretion and bicarbonate synthesis over days
options.B: Renal blood flow is too slow to deliver chemical messages effectively
options.C: Kidneys only operate when the patient is asleep and resting
options.D: Metabolic acids take longer to dissolve in plasma than dissolved gases

explanation: The lungs can change your breathing rate in seconds, but the kidneys need hours to days to manufacture new bicarbonate and adjust what they filter out.

question: What type of lubricant should always be used on a flatus tube before insertion?

options.A: Water-soluble lubricant
options.B: Sterile cooking oil
options.C: Petroleum-based jelly
options.D: Alcohol-based gel

explanation: Water-soluble lubricant is safe for mucous membranes and prevents trauma, unlike petroleum-based products which are harder to clear and can damage tissues. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T11#GNS212_U1_T11_h4)

question: Why are males more commonly affected by X-linked recessive disorders than females?

options.A: The Y chromosome protects female offspring
options.B: Males possess only one X chromosome
options.C: X chromosomes only exist in male bodies
options.D: Females do not have any chromosomes

explanation: Since males only have one X chromosome, a single recessive mutation on that chromosome will express the disease, whereas females have a backup X chromosome. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T15#GNS311_U1_T15_h2)

question: What should you check first if a patient with a catheter suddenly stops passing urine?

options.A: Pull the catheter out right away and put in a new one
options.B: Give a fast dose of an intravenous water pill
options.C: Check the tubing for kinks, twists, or someone lying on it
options.D: Call the doctor to report total kidney failure

explanation: Great nursing instinct! Most of the time, urine stops flowing simply because the tube is bent or pinched. Always check the lines first!

question: A patient recovering from a leg fracture is frustrated and feels like giving up. Which rehabilitation goal addresses this?

options.A: Accelerating the bone fracture healing timeline
options.B: Eliminating the need for any future physical therapy
options.C: Promoting psychological adjustment and coping
options.D: Replacing lost joint cartilage with synthetic tissue

explanation: Recovery is tough mentally too! Supporting patients emotionally and helping them cope is just as important as the physical exercises.

question: What is the best position to place a distressed, breathless patient into right away?

options.A: High Fowler's or sitting upright leaning forward
options.B: Left lateral recovery position
options.C: Flat on the back with legs elevated
options.D: Prone position with a pillow under the chest

explanation: Gravity is our friend here! Sitting upright helps pull the diaphragm down, making it much easier for the patient to draw a breath.

question: A community nurse is mapping health risks in a rural village. What is the best way to find pregnant teenage brides?

options.A: Reviewing national census reports published every ten years
options.B: Partnering with local women leaders and tracking school dropout patterns
options.C: Waiting in urban tertiary hospitals for emergency referrals to arrive
options.D: Relying solely on self-reporting via digital mobile phone surveys

explanation: Local women leaders and school attendance logs give nurses the best grassroots view of which young girls are dropping out and entering marriages.

question: Which of these is the main organ responsible for our sense of touch?

options.A: The spinal cord
options.B: The peripheral nerves
options.C: The skeletal muscles
options.D: The skin

explanation: You've got this! The skin is the body's largest organ and is packed with special nerve endings that help us feel the world around us.

question: Which of these is a key responsibility of a nurse when caring for a suspected victim of violence?

options.A: Issuing formal protection orders to the abuser
options.B: Accurately documenting injuries and maintaining meticulous medical records
options.C: Acting as the presiding judge in court trials
options.D: Arresting the perpetrator at the hospital bedside

explanation: You nailed it! Clear and careful documentation by nurses serves as vital legal evidence in court to protect the patient.

question: In a busy clinic, how does a multi-dose medication vial usually get contaminated?

options.A: Using a previously used needle or syringe to enter the vial
options.B: Cleaning the rubber stopper with alcohol before every puncture
options.C: Storing the medicine bottle inside a warm medication refrigerator
options.D: Failing to shake the suspension liquid before drawing a dose

explanation: That's right! If a needle has touched a patient, using it to enter a shared multi-dose vial contaminates the whole bottle for everyone else. Always use a fresh, sterile needle and syringe! [learn more](GNS122_U4_T2#GNS122_U4_T2_h3)

question: A newborn delivered after a prolonged labor with severe cephalopelvic disproportion is at the highest risk for which condition?

options.A: Primary pulmonary hypertension
options.B: Neural tube closure failure
options.C: Congenital heart defect
options.D: Foetal skull injury

explanation: Prolonged pressure against a tight pelvis creates intense mechanical stress, making the infant very vulnerable to cranial trauma. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T16#GNS121_U6_T16_h2)

question: Which skin-dwelling cell releases histamine when an early inflammation or allergy starts?

options.A: Melanocytes
options.B: Adipocytes
options.C: Mast cells
options.D: Keratinocytes

explanation: Mast cells hold onto histamine and release it when triggered, which kickstarts blood flow and swelling during an inflammatory response.

question: Why are infectious agents like Hepatitis B classified as cancer risk factors?

options.A: They immediately destroy all red blood cells in the body
options.B: They lower body temperature and stop normal digestion
options.C: They block the absorption of vital nutrients in the gut
options.D: They cause chronic inflammation and cellular damage over time

explanation: Certain viruses and bacteria lead to long-term tissue damage and inflammation, which increases the chance of cellular mutations. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T1#GNS321_U1_T1_h4)

question: What advice should you give a patient about sex while she is undergoing treatment for an infection?

options.A: Increase sexual frequency to help flush out the remaining bacteria
options.B: Stop sexual activity only for the first two hours after taking drugs
options.C: Abstain from sexual intercourse until treatment is finished and cure is confirmed
options.D: Continue normal sexual activity as long as condoms are used

explanation: Advise her to pause sexual activity until she finishes her meds and gets the all-clear. This stops reinfection and gives her body time to heal.

question: What is the best position for a woman past 20 weeks pregnant to prevent dizziness from lying flat?

options.A: In a prone position
options.B: Sitting upright with legs dangling
options.C: Flat on her back
options.D: Lateral recumbent position

explanation: Correct! Lying on her side takes the weight of the womb off the main blood vessels, keeping blood flowing smoothly.

question: Why do regular antibiotics like standard penicillin fail against tuberculosis?

options.A: Penicillin only works on viruses, and TB is a fungus
options.B: Human stomach acid destroys penicillin before it reaches the lungs
options.C: The waxy outer cell wall of TB blocks standard drugs from entering
options.D: Tuberculosis bacteria move too fast for penicillin to catch them

explanation: TB bacteria have a tough, waxy outer coat that standard antibiotics just can't break through. That's why special anti-TB drugs are a must!

question: How does keeping a community clean actually help family finances?

options.A: Governments no longer need to collect any domestic taxes
options.B: Families spend less money on medications for preventable illnesses
options.C: Agricultural crop prices drop instantly in local markets
options.D: Hospitals can close down completely due to a lack of patients

explanation: Exactly! When people stay healthy, families save the money they would have spent treating repeated infections.

question: A patient gets a painful, pus-filled swelling where they received an injection days ago. What happened?

options.A: An allergic reaction to the cotton wool used afterward
options.B: A normal immune response to the medication formula
options.C: A localized bacterial infection introduced during the procedure
options.D: Systemic failure of the patient's cardiovascular system

explanation: When hygiene slips, bacteria can hitch a ride on the needle and cause a painful abscess right in the tissue.

question: Which of these is a major warning sign of severe dehydration in a sick child?

options.A: Flushed skin that feels hot to the touch
options.B: An unusually loud and constant cry
options.C: Swelling in both lower legs and feet
options.D: Lethargy or unconsciousness with sunken eyes

explanation: When a child is severely dehydrated, they lose so much fluid that they become very weak, drowsy, or even unconscious, with noticeably sunken eyes. This is an emergency!

question: As a registered nurse working under the team nursing model, what is your primary role on the ward?

options.A: Supervising the doctors during ward rounds
options.B: Performing every single procedure personally for all patients
options.C: Handling only the administrative paperwork for the ward
options.D: Acting as the team leader and taking overall accountability

explanation: Spot on! The registered nurse coordinates the group and takes ultimate responsibility for the care given, even when delegating specific tasks to others. You've got this!

question: A patient scheduled for an intraarticular knee injection mentions taking warfarin daily for a heart condition. What is the nurse's best initial action?

options.A: Notify the healthcare provider about the anticoagulant medication
options.B: Tell the patient to stop taking all heart pills forever
options.C: Administer an extra dose of pain medication immediately
options.D: Scrub the knee with regular soap and water

explanation: Blood thinners increase bleeding risks inside the joint, so the provider must evaluate this before proceeding. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T9#GNS125_U3_T9_h5)

question: Why can't we use very heavy weights with skin traction?

options.A: Heavy weights will damage the skin and slip off
options.B: Skin traction requires a surgical operating room
options.C: Heavy weights make the patient fall asleep faster
options.D: Skin bones cannot support heavy metal devices

explanation: Skin is tough, but it's not made to carry heavy loads! Too much weight will cause blisters, tears, or just slip right out of the straps.

question: At what angle should you insert the needle for an intradermal injection?

options.A: 10 to 15 degrees
options.B: 90 degrees
options.C: 60 degrees
options.D: 45 degrees

explanation: Awesome! A shallow 10 to 15-degree angle is the secret to keeping that needle tip resting nicely right inside the thin dermal layer.

question: What was the major pharmacological breakthrough made by Friedrich Sertürner in 1805?

options.A: Synthesizing aspirin in a laboratory
options.B: Inventing the first hypodermic syringe
options.C: Isolating pure morphine from opium
options.D: Discovering penicillin from a mold

explanation: Friedrich Sertürner isolated morphine from opium, which marked the historical first extraction of an active pure chemical compound from a medicinal plant. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T1#GNS125_U1_T1_h4)

question: Why is poor human resource management dangerous in a hospital setting?

options.A: It automatically lowers the cost of running the hospital
options.B: It leads to increased nurse burnout and medical errors
options.C: It makes doctors work longer shifts in the surgical ward
options.D: It prevents patients from visiting the outpatient department

explanation: When staffing is poorly managed, nurses get overworked and tired. That fatigue can lead to mistakes, which puts our patients at risk. Good HR keeps everyone safe!

question: Why is the risk of infection often lower in home care than in hospital wards?

options.A: Homes are chemically sterilized by professional cleaning crews daily
options.B: Home care nurses wear full surgical hazmat suits during every visit
options.C: Bacteria cannot survive outside of a traditional hospital building
options.D: Patients are separated from other sick individuals and hospital germs

explanation: Recovering away from shared rooms and hospital pathogens greatly reduces the chance of catching secondary infections. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T11#GNS324_U1_T11_h4)

question: You notice on your monthly report that many young clients are skipping their second injectable dose. What is the best action to take?

options.A: Stop ordering injectable contraceptives for the clinic entirely
options.B: Organize community education and strengthen client reminder systems
options.C: Refuse care to any client who misses an appointment date
options.D: Wait until the federal ministry sends a special investigation team

explanation: Wonderful clinical thinking! Spotting a trend like missed doses means we should step up our appointment reminders and patient counseling.

question: Why is emotional and psychological support so important for patients managing celiac disease?

options.A: Mental stress directly converts into physical gluten proteins inside the gut.
options.B: Patients usually develop severe memory loss from carbohydrate withdrawal.
options.C: Strict dietary restriction and social isolation can create significant emotional distress.
options.D: Psychological counseling is the only proven cure for intestinal villous atrophy.

explanation: Living with a lifelong, rigid diet can feel isolating and stressful. Being a warm, supportive nurse makes all the difference for their mental well-being!

question: Why is giving a patient a regular bath or helping them wash up so important in the ward?

options.A: It prevents skin breakdown and infections
options.B: It helps the patient get discharged faster
options.C: It stops doctors from doing morning rounds
options.D: It reduces hospital drug bills

explanation: You're doing great! Regular hygiene washes away harmful germs and dead skin cells, keeping pressure sores and infections far away from your patient.

question: Why must high-risk heart patients take antibiotics before certain dental procedures?

options.A: Dental manipulation can introduce bacteria into the bloodstream, which may latch onto damaged heart valves.
options.B: Dental medications frequently interact negatively with cardiac drugs like digoxin.
options.C: Tooth decay directly causes inflammation of the outer pericardial sac.
options.D: Local anesthetics used by dentists weaken the heart muscle permanently.

explanation: Gum bleeding during dental work lets mouth bacteria sneak into the bloodstream. For a vulnerable heart, prophylactic antibiotics act like a shield!

question: A nurse identifies a case of polio. Why do we place polio in a special, urgent reporting category?

options.A: It is a targeted disease for global eradication and elimination
options.B: It only affects elderly patients in urban hospitals
options.C: It is a common seasonal allergy with mild symptoms
options.D: It does not require tracking by government agencies

explanation: The world is actively trying to wipe out polio completely. Because every single case is a global emergency, we track them with extreme urgency!

question: As you gently bend your patient's neck forward, they automatically bend their knees and hips. What sign is this?

options.A: Normal nuchal flexibility
options.B: A positive Brudzinski's sign
options.C: A negative Kernig's sign
options.D: Early signs of a stroke

explanation: That automatic knee-and-hip-bend when the neck goes forward is a classic positive Brudzinski's sign. It's a clear giveaway for irritated meninges!

question: What term describes the process of putting displaced bone fragments back into their normal alignment?

options.A: Remodeling
options.B: Rehabilitation
options.C: Resection
options.D: Reduction

explanation: Reduction is the medical term for realigning bone ends so they can heal properly, either through closed manipulation or open surgery. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T10#GNS222_U1_T10_h7)

question: Why must a nurse maintain neutrality when counseling patients about genetic risks?

options.A: To allow patients to make their own choices based on personal values
options.B: To prevent patients from asking questions about their family
options.C: To prove that genetics has no real impact on health
options.D: To ensure the hospital avoids paying for laboratory tests

explanation: Reproductive decisions are deeply personal; nurses must guide without imposing personal beliefs or forcing specific choices. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T15#GNS311_U1_T15_h5)

question: A newly admitted patient is too weak to stand on the weighing scale. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Record the weight from their visit five years ago
options.B: Skip the weight measurement until discharge
options.C: Use a bed scale or lift scale for an accurate baseline
options.D: Ask a family member to guess the patient's weight

explanation: Spot on! An accurate baseline weight is key for tracking fluid balance and nutrition, so specialized scales are a lifesaver.

question: Why does secondary adrenal hypofunction usually leave aldosterone production alone?

options.A: Aldosterone is primarily regulated by the renin-angiotensin system, not pituitary ACTH.
options.B: The pituitary gland does not influence any part of the adrenal cortex.
options.C: The adrenal medulla takes over aldosterone production when the pituitary fails.
options.D: Aldosterone is produced in a separate organ outside the adrenal glands.

explanation: Remember that aldosterone answers mostly to your kidneys and blood pressure (via the renin-angiotensin system), not the brain's pituitary gland. So if the pituitary slows down, aldosterone often keeps right on working!

question: Why do we consider pregnant teenagers and malnourished children as high-risk groups?

options.A: They have finished all required community health immunization schedules
options.B: They face a higher probability of poor health outcomes due to biological and social factors
options.C: They always live in urban hospital settings with easy access to doctors
options.D: They consume more public health resources than any other age group

explanation: Vulnerable groups often deal with a mix of body changes, growing needs, and tough living conditions. This makes it easier for them to fall sick, so nurses give them extra care and attention.

question: Which body parts must nurses closely monitor for toxicity when a patient is on aminoglycoside antibiotics?

options.A: Skin and bones
options.B: Brain and spleen
options.C: Kidneys and ears
options.D: Heart and lungs

explanation: Remember 'A-E-I-O-U and sometimes Y', but for aminoglycosides, remember Kidneys (nephrotoxicity) and Ears (ototoxicity)! Keep a close eye on urine output and hearing.

question: Why is it important to check both physical health and mental status when assessing sexual problems?

options.A: Physical illnesses and emotional stress frequently interact to impair sexual function
options.B: Physical causes are always temporary while psychological ones are permanent
options.C: Medical insurance will not pay for treatment without both evaluations
options.D: Psychological causes can never be treated with medication

explanation: The body and mind work as a team. Good sexual health needs healthy blood vessels, steady hormones, and peace of mind all working together.

question: What must you ensure before sending an emergency obstetric patient on a long ambulance ride?

options.A: The patient has signed discharge papers against medical advice
options.B: All routine hospital laundry duties have been fully completed
options.C: A family member has paid the complete transport fare in cash
options.D: The patient is stabilized and secure intravenous access is established

explanation: Always make sure your patient is as stable as possible with a working IV line so you can give fluids or meds during transit.
